title: Client abort handling and partial-generation garbage collection
creator: Anika Rao
description: When clients abort streaming requests (explicit cancel, TCP reset, or long client-side timeouts) we currently leave partially-produced outputs, transient KV cache entries, and ephemeral allocation tied to the stream alive for the full server-side TTL. This leads to elevated memory usage, continued CPU/GPU allocations for stuck generations, and incorrect billing/observability signals. This ticket standardizes abort detection, introduces a fast-path cleanup for partial generations, and establishes a deterministic garbage-collection policy for orphaned stream state.
background: Incidents and internal dashboards show recurring spikes in memory and GPU kernel activity correlated with aborted streaming sessions. User-reported problems include: truncated or duplicated outputs on retry, delayed resource reclamation, and confusing billing entries when tokens were generated but never delivered. Existing related work focused on reconciling fragments (ENG-23109) and abrupt disconnect pruning (ENG-17012) but does not provide a single lifecycle or explicit GC for partial generations tied to API semantics like structured outputs and function/tool calls.
proposal: 1) Add a client-abort sentinel that is set when the transport layer signals a disconnect or an explicit cancel from SDKs. 2) Implement an in-runtime partial-generation finalizer that: a) halts active token generation for the stream, b) runs a compact finalization step to emit a deterministic partial response (if possible) tagged as "partial: true" to logs and internal telemetry only, c) releases KV cache and per-stream memory immediately, and d) writes an audit event for billing and troubleshooting. 3) Introduce a conservative orphan GC that reclaims streams with no activity after short grace period (configurable, default 8s) and an aggressive GC for low-memory situations (2s). 4) For structured outputs and tool calls, ensure any external invocation is either rolled back or marked in the audit trail so downstream systems can reconcile. 5) Add SDK-level best-practice guidance for client-side backoff and cancel semantics to reduce orphan rates.
acceptance_criteria: Server reclaims >95% of per-stream memory within 1s of detecting abort on synthetic tests
No increase in user-visible latency for healthy streaming requests (<= 1% regression in p50) after changes
All partial-generation finalizer events are recorded to audit log with stream_id, cause, and truncated_token_count
Structured-output tool invocations are either completed or left in a reconciliable state with explicit audit entries
E2E tests for reconnect+resume and abort+retry demonstrate deterministic behavior and correct billing attribution
implementation_steps: Instrument transport to emit standardized abort reasons (CLIENT_CANCEL, TCP_RESET, READ_TIMEOUT, PROTOCOL_ERROR)
Add stream lifecycle state machine transition for ABORTING -> FINALIZED_ABORT that triggers finalizer
Implement finalizer routine: stop generation, flush lightweight summary event, free KV cache slots, decrement resource accounting
Expose config flags: stream_grace_period_ms (default 8000), aggressive_gc_threshold_ms (default 2000) and metrics toggles
Integrate with billing pipeline: tag tokens generated after abort sentinel and ensure they are either discount-credited or flagged for manual review
Add structured-output hooks: when a tool call is in-flight, mark call as "orphanable" and emit reconciliation keys so downstream workers can roll back or retry safely
SDK changes: provide cancel() with guaranteed server notification and example retry patterns in node/python SDKs
Create canary on dedicated cluster with tracing enabled to validate behavior under production load
testing_plan: Unit tests for state machine transitions and finalizer correctness
Integration tests simulating TCP resets, SDK cancels, and slow clients with variable read timeouts
Chaos test: inject network partitions and ensure GC recovers orphan streams without impacting unrelated requests
Performance regression tests: compare p50/p95/p99 latencies pre/post change using production-like traces
Billing test: synthetic traffic where half of streams abort and validate tokens credited/flagged per policy
End-to-end structured output test: simulate tool invocation mid-stream abort and verify reconciliation markers are present
rollback_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag. If we see >1% regression on healthy traffic or any data loss in structured-output reconciliation, flip the flag to disable finalizer and revert config to previous TTLs. Emergency runbook: re-enable older GC path and scale dedicated clusters to free resources while we investigate.
